rationale: Evidence from iteration 6 (score 927.4, best so far). Oval (20/20 finishes, 1.86 s, rms 0.004) and s-bend (20/20, 2.10 s) are near their ceiling. The slalom is the remaining gap: 19/20 finishes, one off-track exit, 0.98 progress, 1.0 line-loss events per run, and finishing runs take 2.48 s. Moving the sensors forward from y=0.07 to y=0.08 lifted slalom finishes from 16/20 to 19/20, which supports the late-reaction hypothesis (H6). Each line-loss event costs 15 points on every track, and each off-track exit costs about 500 points, so the priority is fewer line losses on the slalom. This iteration makes two changes. (1) kd 1.0 to 1.2 for more damping of the faster corrections. Oval steering_oscillation is 0.21, so there is room for more damping without much jitter. (2) Mass 0.6 to 0.5 kg to reduce yaw inertia and speed up correction. The mass is at the low end of its range and the drive is not expected to be grip-limited at these speeds. Sensors (y=0.08, span +/-0.045 m), weights, kp 2.0, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.0, line_loss and the other geometry are unchanged, so the effect can be attributed. Expected result: slalom finishes 19/20 or 20/20, line_loss_events falling from about 1.0 toward 0.5 or less on the slalom, oval and s-bend unchanged near 945 and 940, and slalom time near 2.4 s. Risks: kd 1.2 could add jitter on the oval, and lower mass could make the robot more sensitive to the motor mismatch. Hypotheses: H8, more damping reduces the line-loss events from overshoot on alternating bends; H9, lower mass shortens the correction time enough to cut slalom off-track exits. Measurements wanted next: slalom completion and line_loss_events to test H8 and H9; steering_oscillation on all tracks to check kd jitter; completion_time on the oval and s-bend to confirm the time budget at base_speed 1.0.
